identity_note: Package identity is (package_id, schema_version), NOT the generation date. Re-generating on a later date without a content change does not produce a new package. Financials certification should yield alloy-context.v1.1 — a compatible revision — unless including it requires a schema change, in which case v2.
tier1_cap_note: Tier 1 is capped at five documents. Raising the cap is a ratified decision, not an editorial one: the validator fails if the foundation set grows without this number changing in the same commit.

foundation.role: the current platform in one document
foundation.authority: synthesis — owns nothing; every section defers to a domain owner
foundation.why_global: it is the only document that describes the whole implemented platform at once, so it is what stops a lane-scoped agent reasoning from a partial model
foundation.staleness_trigger: any domain certification state change; a change to the core model, authority layering or canonical URL bases

foundation.why_global: the forbidden list is the accumulated record of mistakes actually made against this codebase; without it an agent repeats them
foundation.staleness_trigger: a new certified safe inference; any newly documented wrong inference

foundation.role: one concern, one owner, plus the staleness contract
foundation.authority: routing authority — decides which document is authority for a concern
foundation.why_global: it turns Tier 2 selection into a lookup instead of a guess, and names the deliberate non-owners
foundation.staleness_trigger: an owner change; a concern gaining a second claimant; a domain certified or de-certified

foundation.role: per-domain certification manifest and the status scoreboard
foundation.why_global: it is where certification state and per-domain debt live; an agent must know what is NOT certified
foundation.staleness_trigger: every domain certification wave; any manifest version bump

foundation.why_global: cheap, and prevents term drift between operator language and schema language

update_triggers: any lane recertification trigger firing (see recertification-triggers.json)
a domain moving between certified and pending
a Tier 1 document changing, being added or being removed
a canonical owner changing for any concern
a document changing volatility class — which happens whenever measured counts are added to static doctrine
